question: How does flexibility of the cell membrane help living organisms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Absorbs food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The flexibility of the cell membrane allows **cells to engulf nutrients** from their surroundings through a process called **endocytosis**.
 
• It enables the transport of essential molecules like glucose, amino acids, and ions into the cell, ensuring proper **cellular function**.
 
• The cell membrane’s dynamic nature supports **selective permeability**, allowing the absorption of beneficial substances while excluding harmful ones.
 
• This property helps cells in maintaining **homeostasis**, which is vital for their survival and function.
 
• Flexibility also aids in cellular communication by facilitating the interaction of membrane receptors with external signals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Membrane Structure:** The cell membrane is composed of a **phospholipid bilayer** with embedded proteins, making it semi-permeable and flexible.
 
• **Endocytosis:** A process where cells absorb external materials by engulfing them within vesicles formed from the cell membrane.
 
• **Selective Permeability:** The ability of the membrane to allow certain molecules to pass through while blocking others, crucial for nutrient absorption and waste removal.
 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model:** This model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic structure where lipids and proteins can move laterally, ensuring its flexibility and functionality.
 
• **Homeostasis:** The cell membrane plays a key role in maintaining the internal balance of the cell by regulating the exchange of substances with its environment.
